observed_facts: HMCV1-SASC-01 Stage P terminated at 240017.765 ms with provider/transport failure.
HMCV1-SASC-10 Stage P terminated at 240026.322 ms with provider/transport failure.
No Stage P provider output existed and Stage C was never called.
Two calls were consumed, with no retries, repairs, or selections.
Both host traces retained their initial inference_started=false value because the runner lifecycle file was inside a deleted temporary directory.

The frozen tokenizer-only preflight proved 131072-token trie construction and canonical stream projectability, but its enhanced whole-stream check increased measured work from about 1.8 seconds to about 30.7 seconds.
Earlier shorter Gate F constrained responses completed in roughly 29–45 seconds, so the shared model/provider path is capable of completing bounded constrained generation.
not_established: Whether either timed-out runner completed tokenizer loading, trie construction, model loading, prompt tokenization, or any generated token.
Whether the timeout was caused primarily by model loading, constrained-token projection, generated length, failure to reach EOS, WSL/GPU state, or an interaction among them.
Whether 1400 output tokens are necessary, excessive, or insufficient.
Whether increasing the 240-second timeout would produce a terminal ledger.
Any semantic capability result for either proof case.

causal_hypotheses_ranked.hypothesis: Stage P's longer structured output amplifies the current callback's full-prefix decode and full DFA replay on every generated token, producing approximately quadratic prefix-processing work.
causal_hypotheses_ranked.evidence: The runner decodes all generated IDs and reconstructs State().feed(decoded) on every prefix callback; the tokenizer-only canonical whole-stream exercise materially increased preflight time.

causal_hypotheses_ranked.hypothesis: The model did not reach a terminal ledger before the generous 1400-token ceiling or wall-clock timeout because Stage P permits up to eight verbose entries and multiple free-text fields.
causal_hypotheses_ranked.evidence: No token-progress or terminal-state evidence survived; the output contract is substantially longer than Gate F.

causal_hypotheses_ranked.hypothesis: One or more fixed startup phases, including model load or WSL/GPU initialization, consumed most of the timeout.
causal_hypotheses_ranked.evidence: Runner lifecycle evidence was lost, so startup completion is unknown; identical near-exact timeouts are consistent with any nonterminal phase.

requirements: Allocate a case-bound append-only lifecycle directory outside every TemporaryDirectory before launching WSL.
Persist host launch identity, request identity, runner identity, PID when available, monotonic start time, deadline, timeout, termination result, and exit state.
Runner emits exclusively-created, monotonically numbered event records; no lifecycle file is overwritten.

Required events: RUNNER_STARTED, REQUEST_VALIDATED, TOKENIZER_LOAD_STARTED/COMPLETED, TRIE_BUILD_STARTED/COMPLETED, PREWARM_STARTED/COMPLETED, MODEL_LOAD_STARTED/COMPLETED, PROMPT_TOKENIZED, GENERATION_STARTED, GENERATION_HEARTBEAT, TERMINAL_EOS, RESPONSE_PERSISTED, RUNNER_EXCEPTION.

Generation heartbeat every 16 emitted tokens or 10 seconds, whichever occurs first, binds token count, decoded UTF-8 byte count/hash, DFA mode, entry count, trie cache size, latest allowed-token count, and elapsed phase time.
Persist quarantined partial generated bytes or an append-only byte/hash checkpoint before each heartbeat so timeout evidence is not reduced to counters.
Raw or partial output is never parsed as complete, repaired, resumed, or granted semantic authority.
Host timeout records whether graceful termination and forced termination were attempted and observed.
remediation_stage_1_durable_observabilit.privacy_and_authority: Lifecycle evidence contains only the already-governed case input identities and quarantined model output; it grants no factual, curriculum, runtime, or training authority.

requirements: Use the unchanged frozen tokenizer and DFA/trie identities.
Measure tokenizer load, token-piece extraction, trie build, prewarm, and prefix-callback simulation separately.
Exercise canonical COMPLETE and INDETERMINATE ledgers at one, four, and eight entries with short and maximum-bounded free strings.
Record per-prefix and cumulative latency, DFA replay characters, cache hits/misses, allowed-token counts, memory high-water mark, and terminal EOS reachability.
Compare the current full-prefix replay algorithm with a candidate incremental tracker without executing a model.

Incremental tracking may feed only the decoded suffix when the new decoded prefix byte-exactly extends the prior prefix; any retokenization divergence must rebuild from the immutable full prefix or fail closed, never guess.
Prove identical allowed-token sets between current and incremental algorithms for all sampled prefixes and randomized valid/invalid ledgers before considering replacement.
acceptance: Zero invalid terminal streams accepted and zero canonical streams blocked.
No model/provider import, load, or call.
Enough timing evidence to attribute expected wall-clock cost by phase before changing timeout or output ceiling.

allowed_only_if_stage_2_supports_it: Replace full DFA replay with the proven equivalent incremental/rebuild tracker.
Move lifecycle storage outside temporary directories.
Add deterministic progress and terminal receipts.
prohibited_without_new_design_authority: No prompt, schema, enum, entry-limit, completeness, source-membership, model, tokenizer, quantization, or sampling change.
Do not increase timeout or reduce max output tokens merely to obtain a result.
No partial-ledger acceptance, continuation, retry, repair, or resumption.
No Stage C, Gate S, Core/Voice runtime, curriculum, or training change.

verification_sequence_before_any_proof_r: Implement durable lifecycle boundary and test forced timeout with a non-model synthetic child process.
Run zero-inference real-tokenizer characterization and equivalence tests.
Freeze candidate identities and stop for owner review.
If separately authorized, run one Stage-P-only Case 01 diagnostic call with no Stage C and no retry.
Require complete durable lifecycle, terminal constrained output, strict ledger/source validation, and measured phase timings.
Only after Case 01 infrastructure success may a separate Case 10 Stage-P-only diagnostic be considered.
The full two-case Stage P/Stage C proof requires later fresh authority; unused calls from failed Run 1 are not reusable authority.
design_conclusion: Do not adjust the timeout first. The narrowest next engineering work is durable lifecycle capture followed by zero-inference callback-cost characterization and equivalence proof. This distinguishes infrastructure latency from semantic failure at lower evidence cost than another model run.
